claims.text: Microsoft's Azure business crossed $100 billion in revenue; Azure's full fiscal-year 2026 revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time (Microsoft fiscal Q4 2026, ended June 30, 2026), per Microsoft.
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion, up from $106 billion a year earlier.
AWS's AI business and its chips business (including Trainium and Graviton) each exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate, growing triple-digit percentages year-over-year.
AWS posted $42.2 billion revenue in Q2 2026, up 37% year-over-year, accelerating from 28% growth the prior quarter, its fastest growth since 2021.
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in fiscal Q4 2026, up from 40% the prior quarter.
Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chairman and CEO, said: "This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time."
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capex guidance to $195–205 billion, up from an earlier $180–190 billion estimate that had already been raised twice this year.

Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion, up 39% year-over-year; remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up 363% year-over-year; prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals total $75 billion.
Gartner forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
Gartner says by 2028 cloud-native platforms will be the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives, up from less than 50% in 2023.
In Pulumi's 2026 survey of 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers, 64% run on AWS, 55% on Google Cloud, and 45% on Azure.
Gartner forecasts total worldwide AI spending to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026, a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents.
Gartner predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms, with spending on securing AI reaching roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
Gartner predicts by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams.

CNCF's Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData found 28% of surveyed organizations have a dedicated platform engineering team and 35% run a hybrid platform combining existing developer platforms with AI tooling.
Chris Aniszczyk, CTO of CNCF, said cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are standardizing on CNCF projects, and organizations are extending platforms to support AI workloads.
Gartner predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029, while human-in-the-loop requirements fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.

Pulumi's 2026 survey found 82% agree AI agents will change how they write infrastructure within 12 months; 63% say they trust agents to make production changes while manual approval remains close to universal; teams expecting agents to generate half or more of infrastructure code rise from 45% to 52% within six months.
Pulumi's report describes the gap as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
Pulumi Neo proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails.
Mordor Intelligence says the global Kubernetes market is valued at USD 3.13 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031, a 21.85% CAGR.

CNCF's Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%, and 30% of backend developers using Kubernetes directly, down from a peak of 36% in Q3 2023, which the report attributes to maturity.
The July 2026 revision of the Model Context Protocol is described by its maintainers as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit; Mirantis's Lens launched a built-in MCP server.
Gartner says by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use AI code assistants, and 63% of organizations are piloting, deploying or beginning to use them.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes.
The 2026 predictions from last year's edition held up.
McKinsey's report says cloud value from innovation is worth 5x more than cost savings and EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030 for high performers.
